source_text: Nam cum tu et Manichaeus dicitis: Omnes sunt naturaliter peccatores, Apostolus autem dicit: Multi sunt, non omnes peccatores, removet accusationem a seminibus, quae armatur in mores, et destruit originale peccatum. Utque hoc ipsum, quod egimus, urgeamus: praescribit Apostolus multos debere intellegi per Adae inoboedientiam peccatores, multos autem per Christi oboedientiam iustos eos utique, qui iusti sunt, ostendens ab illis, qui criminosi sunt, esse discretos; tu quia impudentia argumentari niteris, ut ex his sermonibus probes naturale peccatum? Nam cum dicis omnes nasci criminosos per Adam et propter hoc ad diabolum pertinere, sed aliquos inde per Christum postea liberari, non hoc sentis, quod Apostolus, qui dicit non omnes per Adam peccatores constitutos esse, sed multos.
pass_a_gloss: For when you and a Manichaean say: All are naturally sinners, but the Apostle says: Many are, not all, sinners, he removes an accusation from seeds, which is armed against manners, and destroys original sin. And that we may urge this itself which we have done: the Apostle prescribes that many ought to be understood as sinners through Adam's disobedience, but many just through Christ's obedience, showing those namely who are just as having been discreted from those who are criminal; you, because you strive to argue by shamelessness, so that from these speeches you may prove a natural sin? For when you say that all are born criminal through Adam and on this account belong to the devil, but that some from there are afterward freed through Christ, you do not mean this which the Apostle, who says that not all were constituted sinners through Adam, but many.

lemmas.lexica: LS semen; Blaise bodily seed vs transmitted sin
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: For while you and the Manichaean say, ‘All are sinners by nature,’ the apostle says, ‘Many, not all, are sinners’ (Romans 5:19). He removes from seed the accusation armed against conduct, and destroys original sin. Let us press this same point. The apostle directs us to understand that many are sinners through Adam’s disobedience and many righteous through Christ’s obedience, showing that those who are righteous are distinct from those who are criminal. With what shamelessness do you struggle to argue that these words prove natural sin? When you say all are born guilty through Adam and therefore belong to the devil, but that some are afterward freed from this through Christ, you do not mean what the apostle means: he says not all but many were made sinners through Adam.

choices.why: Bodily seed of generation; Julian denies it carries a will's sin.
Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.

Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.
